summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at W.A.C.A. Ground commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 403/10 (115.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Australia countered with 662/9 (179.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Steve Smith 239 (400b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Steve Smith delivered a masterclass for Australia (239 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 64%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by DJ Malan (194 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by innings & 41 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
